sections.html:
Opelika serves as the seat of Lee County in east central Alabama and pairs with Auburn to anchor one metro area. The city stands about 807 feet above sea level and covers roughly 62 square miles. ZIP codes run from 36801 to 36804.

Population reached 30,995 in the 2020 census, a gain of 17.1 percent over 2010, and the latest estimate is 35,765. Auburn adjoins the city and the Columbus, Georgia area lies within commuting range, so buyers come from three directions: people who work in Opelika, people who work in Auburn and people who drive toward Columbus.

East Alabama Health employs more than 3,700 people. New industry investment since 2005 has topped $2.6 billion and added over 4,700 jobs. If an employer is expanding near your street, say so, and give commute times.

Few owner-occupied homes sit empty, so houses in decent shape tend to draw interest. One that needs heavy work narrows the field, and that is the gap an as-is buyer fills.

Opelika grew up around the railroad. The Montgomery and West Point Railroad made it a cotton shipping point, the town received its charter on February 9, 1854, and the city nearly doubled between 1870 and 1900. Homes built during that boom are now far older than a century.

An inspector will study the framing, wiring and plumbing in one of them. Fixes at that age seldom stay small, and plenty of owners decide to sell as is instead of starting the work.

Opelika has a mayor and council government. Voters elect the mayor at large for four years, the mayor holds full executive power including hiring and dismissing department heads, and a five member council works beside the office. Permits, code questions and utility accounts all run through city departments, so phone the right office before deciding a rule does or does not cover your house.

If a previous owner added a room or finished a space without a permit, ask the city what clearing it would take. A buyer's lender or inspector may raise it later.

Public amenities give a listing something to point to. Spring Villa Park spreads over 350 acres with trails, disc golf and camping. The SportsPlex and Aquatics Center cost $32 million and opened in 2009, the pickleball facility has 24 courts and opened in 2019, and the library cost $12 million and opened in 2021. A short drive to any of them is a fair talking point.

Opelika City Schools operates nine schools: three primary schools for kindergarten through grade 2, three intermediate schools for grades 3 to 5, a sixth grade school, a middle school for grades 7 and 8 and Opelika High School for grades 9 to 12. With grades spread over several buildings, a family will want the assigned schools named for the address. Southern Union State Community College has a campus in town and Auburn University is close.

Interstate 85, US 29, US 280, US 431 and Alabama State Routes 14 and 51 all reach the city, and Lee-Russell Public Transit runs dial-a-ride. Because the city sprawls, the trip to the interstate differs a lot between addresses. State the real distance in your description.

Under Alabama Code section 40-22-1, a deed carries a recordation tax of 50 cents per $500 of value, paid before the probate judge records it. It appears on the closing statement beside a recording fee.

Property tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. Lee County offices hold parcel records and can quote the current balance. Because a fall sale may land right when the new bill arrives, settle in the contract who covers it, and check that the closing statement shows the split.

After you accept an offer, a title company or attorney researches ownership, looks for liens and sets a closing date with you. At the table you sign the deed and the settlement statement. The closer pays off any mortgage and tax balance out of the proceeds and hands you what remains.

Bring a photo ID, the deed or estate paperwork, your lender's payoff information and, for a rental, the lease. If something unexpected appears in the title search, ask what it will cost to clear and decide whether to proceed. You are not obligated until you sign.

sections.h2: Getting the house ready to show
sections.html:
You do not need a renovation, but a few cheap steps make any buyer take you seriously. Clear out trash and clutter, open the blinds, and make sure water, power and gas are on so the buyer can test the systems. If the roof leaks or the air conditioning is dead, say so up front instead of hoping it goes unnoticed.

Photographs help even in a cash sale. Take pictures of every room, the roof, the water heater and the electrical panel, and note any known problem beside the photo. A buyer who sees the whole picture makes a firmer offer and is less likely to renegotiate later.

If the house is vacant, confirm the insurance still covers it. Many policies change their terms when a home sits empty, and a claim denied on an empty house can cost far more than a quick sale.

Ask each buyer to put the offer in writing and to say who pays closing costs. Check whether the offer depends on an inspection, a loan or an appraisal, because those conditions are where a deal falls apart. A cash offer with no financing condition removes the biggest one.

Ask how fast the buyer can close and whether that date is firm. Then compare the net you would receive from each route: a cash sale, a repaired listing and a listing as is. Include repair costs, agent fees, tax and utility bills during the wait, and the stress of keeping a house show-ready.

sections.h2: When a cash offer suits an Opelika house
sections.html:
Cash works for sellers who value certainty over a long marketing period. Typical Opelika situations:

  • A house near downtown with outdated electrical, plumbing or roofing.
  • An inherited property the family wants settled.
  • A rental with deferred maintenance or a tenant who stopped paying.
  • A sale that must happen before a move to or from the Auburn or Columbus area.

Weigh an offer against what a listing could net after repairs, agent fees and months of waiting. About 174,000 people live in the Auburn-Opelika metro area, so the local buyer pool has limits, and a house needing work can wait a long time for the right person.

The steps are few. Describe the house, receive our offer, and decide. Cleaning and repairs are not required before closing. We buy Opelika houses as they stand, and you can decline any offer.

An inherited house adds a step. The person signing must show legal authority to sell, so speak with the probate office or an attorney before requesting offers. Find the deed if you can, along with the last tax bill and a list of what the house needs.

A rented house adds another. Share the lease, the rent history and whether the tenant plans to stay. Cash buyers can close with a tenant in place or after move-out, whichever you prefer.

faqs.q: Must I fix up an Opelika house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer takes the house in its current condition, so repairs and cleaning are not required.
